themes.text: Agents are moving faster than the checks around them, and attackers now exploit new flaws within days of disclosure.
Arabica tops $3 a pound while roasting quietly electrifies, from $2,995 fluid-bed machines to solar heat stored in rock.
A 20-year-old wins Il Lombardia, Lachlan Morton outrides the Pony Express, and new gravel world champions are crowned in Australia.
Paris flights may be hit Oct 17–21, ETIAS still isn't open (skip the paid look-alike sites), and new nonstops reach Costa Rica and Iceland.

desks.title: Technology
desks.blurb: The most important moves in AI, security and the infrastructure that runs it, with the original reporting linked.

items.head: Meta launches Muse Wonder frontier models
items.text: Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full target agent work, long-term memory and coding, and are available through the Meta Model API and Muse Code. Meta's benchmark claims have not yet been tested independently.

items.head: OpenAI pulls three of its 722 AI-written math papers
items.text: OpenAI posted the papers from an unreleased internal model on Oct 6 and withdrew three a day later over a sign error. Many mathematicians criticized the release for skipping verification.

items.head: White House announces $6 billion in science initiatives
items.text: Eleven companies pledged $2.4 billion in computing credits and AI tools for DOE's Genesis Mission, including $1 billion from Nvidia, $500 million from AMD and $200 million from OpenAI.

items.head: Microsoft adds execution containers for AI agents
items.text: Windows gains local AI models and Microsoft Execution Containers, which restrict the data agents can access. The premium Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599.

items.head: Critical SonicWall SMA 1000 flaw under attack
items.text: CVE-2026-102255 (CVSS 10.0) is a pre-auth SSRF patched on Oct 6. Previdian has seen 135 exploitation attempts from two US IP addresses. SonicWall's advisory does not yet list active exploitation.

items.head: Atlassian Data Center flaw now exploited
items.text: CVE-2026-21589 (CVSS 9.3) drew exploitation attempts within two hours of public details, and watchTowr confirms in-the-wild exploitation. It affects Jira, Confluence, Bitbucket and other Data Center products.

items.head: Public exploit gives root on AnyDesk for Linux 8.0.2
items.text: The pre-auth exploit works over direct TCP connections on port 7070. AnyDesk fixed the bug in 8.0.3 in June without a CVE or advisory, so check Linux hosts are updated.

items.head: FBI and Secret Service warn about FortiBleed
items.text: A credential-harvesting campaign targets internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways. No CVE has been assigned. SOCRadar counts 86,644 compromised devices in 194 countries, and attackers sometimes change or delete the original admin accounts.

items.head: Microsoft unveils Azure Maia 300
items.text: Maia 200 is in production across the US, Europe and Australia. Maia 300 racks of 96 accelerators at 167kW arrive in 2027, and Microsoft claims up to 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems.

items.head: Oracle trucks in natural gas to keep data centers running
items.text: Bloomberg reports Oracle has trucked compressed gas to its Salt Lake City site for over a year while waiting for a pipeline, and is considering the same for its stalled Project Jupiter in New Mexico.

items.head: FERC approves PJM data center database
items.text: PJM will track each site's location, power providers, ramp-up and backup generation. FERC rejected a separate plan to cut grid power to data centers during peak stress.

items.head: Data center fires and power failures have doubled since 2024
items.text: The Energy Incident Register counts 8 in 2024, 20 in 2025 and 19 so far in 2026. UPS systems and battery rooms are the most common named failure point.

desks.title: Coffee
desks.blurb: What is moving the coffee business, and the shift from gas drum roasters to electric roasting.

sections.title: Industry and markets
sections.blurb: Prices, companies and rules that shape the cup.

items.head: Arabica climbs above $3 a pound
items.text: A stronger Brazilian real pushed arabica past US$3/lb before prices gave back gains. Brazil's September exports rose over 20% year on year, and US forecasters expect one of the strongest El Niños in 75 years.

items.head: Coca-Cola reportedly revisits a Costa Coffee sale
items.text: Costa is back in profit on £1.3bn in revenue, and sources say Coca-Cola is again exploring a sale after earlier bids fell short of its valuation.

items.head: Nespresso drops its compostable paper capsules
items.text: Nespresso is ending the home-compostable capsules sold in 14 European markets, citing short shelf life and customer feedback, and will focus on aluminum.

sections.title: Electric roasting watch
sections.blurb: Machines and experiments moving roasting off gas.

items.head: Sandia tests stored solar heat for drum roasters
items.text: Sandia National Laboratories and Albuquerque's Michael Thomas Coffee stored solar electricity as heat in a rock bed and fed it to a drum roaster, reaching 600°C. The goal is a bolt-on retrofit that cuts gas use.

items.head: Coffee Crafters ships the all-electric Duo
items.text: A compact fluid-bed roaster for 200 grams to 2 pounds a batch, up to 10 pounds an hour, on 240-volt power. It starts at $2,995.

items.head: Rex Roaster's 4-pound electric drum plugs into 120 volts
items.text: The manual, stainless machine runs on a standard 20-amp outlet, works with Artisan profiling software and lists at $6,000.

items.head: SCAJ World Specialty Coffee Conference, Tokyo
items.text: Japan's specialty coffee show runs under the theme "Brew The Future."

items.head: Coffee Fest Dallas-Fort Worth
items.text: More than 50 free seminars plus paid workshops, close to home for Texas roasters and café owners.

desks.title: Cycling
desks.blurb: Big rides and races in the US and worldwide, plus where to buy and service your bike.

sections.title: Racing and rides
sections.blurb: The stories riders are talking about.

items.head: Lachlan Morton beats the 1861 Pony Express record
items.text: Morton rode 1,998 miles from St. Joseph, Missouri to Sacramento in 6 days, 21 hours and 15 minutes, beating the horseback record by 19 hours 45 minutes.

items.head: Paul Seixas, 20, becomes youngest Il Lombardia winner
items.text: The Frenchman won the season's last Monument solo, his first Monument victory. Tadej Pogačar did not start.

items.head: Gravel worlds: Bak Klaris and Vos take the rainbow jerseys
items.text: Denmark's Magnus Bak Klaris won the men's 144 km race in Nannup, Western Australia, and Marianne Vos took her second gravel world title, her 15th world title overall.

sections.title: Ride and race calendar
sections.blurb: US and world events coming up.

items.head: UCI Track World Championships, Shanghai
items.text: About 400 riders from some 45 nations race for 22 world titles, with points toward the LA 2028 Olympics.

items.head: Big Sugar Gravel, Bentonville, Arkansas
items.text: The 100- and 50-mile routes were still open for registration at last check; elite fields are closed.

items.head: 2027 Tour de France route revealed in Paris
items.text: The route is announced live; the 2027 race starts in Edinburgh on July 2, Scotland's first Grand Départ.

items.head: Texas MS 150: Houston and Austin to College Station
items.text: Two-day ride with starts in Houston and Austin, an overnight in La Grange and the finish in College Station.

desks.title: Travel
desks.blurb: What affects your next trip, the rules and safety basics to check first, where to go, and offers worth a look.

items.head: French flight crews file strike notice for Oct 17–21
items.text: About 36,000 crew are covered, with Air France, Transavia and Corsair most exposed. No cancellations announced yet, and the notice could be lifted. Check your airline 48 to 72 hours before flying.

items.head: New nonstops to Costa Rica, Austin–San Jose and St. Louis–Iceland
items.text: Breeze now flies Tampa to San José, Costa Rica, its first Central America route. Delta added daily Austin to San Jose, California, and Icelandair adds seasonal St. Louis service from May 2027.

sections.title: Restrictions and entry rules
sections.blurb: Advisories, entry permits and health notices to check before you book.

items.head: Don't pay for ETIAS yet: Europe isn't taking applications
items.text: More than 150 sites reportedly sell ETIAS applications for €50 to €178, but the EU system isn't open and has no launch date. Use only the official EU site once it opens.

items.head: Americans need a UK ETA before flying to Britain
items.text: The electronic travel authorisation costs £20 on GOV.UK, covers visits of up to six months, and every traveler needs one, including children. Unofficial sites charge more.

items.head: CDC: reconsider travel to Ebola areas of eastern DR Congo
items.text: A Level 3 notice covers Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces. Level 2 precautions apply to the rest of DR Congo and Uganda.

items.head: Lonely Planet names its Best in Travel 2027
items.text: The 25 picks include Okinawa, Oman, Šibenik, Bariloche, Da Nang and Rabat, plus US choices Maryland, New Mexico and the Northern California redwood coast.

sections.title: Safety and smart-travel tips
sections.blurb: Simple habits that save money and trouble.

items.head: Enroll in STEP before any international trip
items.text: The State Department's free Smart Traveler program emails embassy alerts for your destination and helps the embassy reach you in an emergency.

items.head: Buy entry permits only on government sites
items.text: Look-alike sites charge several times the real fee for UK ETAs and EU permits. Skip sponsored search results and go to GOV.UK or the official EU site directly.

items.head: Get TSA PreCheck to keep shoes and laptop in place
items.text: Enrolled travelers keep shoes, belts, laptops and liquids in their bags at screening. Enrollment costs $77.95 to $85 depending on the provider.

items.head: Check health notices before you book
items.text: CDC lists outbreaks and recommended precautions by destination, from malaria to chikungunya. Some need vaccines or medicine weeks before you leave.

sections.title: Deals worth a look
sections.blurb: Check terms and dates before booking.

items.head: United offers status match to Delta and American members
items.text: Elite members can match status and keep it through January 2028 by flying and spending within 90 days.

items.head: Princess Hotels: up to 42% off in Punta Cana and Riviera Maya
items.text: For travel through March 28, 2027.

items.head: Uniworld: $500 to $1,500 off 2027 river cruises
items.text: Includes Milan to Venice, Portugal and Spain, and Budapest to Passau itineraries.
